scope: Proposition 3.4 (Relative klt programs over a compact base) of the manuscript “Log abundance for compact Kähler spaces under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity” (preprints/Log-abundance-for-compact-Kahler-spaces-under-logarithmic-Iitaka-subadditivity-October-6-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 46adc5be1070213b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let π : T → V be projective bimeromorphic, where V is a normal compact Kähler space and T is normal, compact Kähler, and globally strongly Q-factorial. Let (T, B) be an effective rational klt pair with rational-line adjoint J = KT + B. There is a finite sequence of ordinary J-negative steps over V , all projective over V , whose last adjoint is curve-nef over V , meaning that it has nonnegative degree on every curve contracted over V . Every working space is compact Kähler and globally strongly Q-factorial. On a common resolution the comparison from the first adjoint to the last is effective and exceptional over the last space.
